items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a popular geography YouTube Shorts channel. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller: brisk and curious, with natural emphasis and a short comic pause before each punchline. Chars voices funny cartoon characters, short and punchy: a smug, proud warm ocean current (lines 7 and 18), then a slow deadpan defensive mountain range (line 15).
lines: Narrator
London is further north than all forty-eight mainland US states.
Narrator
Yet in January, New York is colder. By about five degrees.
Narrator
Same with Calgary. London's latitude. Minus eight... versus plus five.
Narrator
So why is Europe so warm?
Narrator
Ask anyone, and they'll point here. The Gulf Stream.
Narrator
A warm current, flowing from the Gulf of Mexico all the way to Europe.
Chars
[smug, proud] Central heating. You're welcome, Europe.
Narrator
But in two thousand two, scientists at Columbia University ran the numbers.
Narrator
The ocean's heat warms Europe by just a few degrees. And it warms America's side too.
Narrator
So where does the rest of the gap come from?
Narrator
The wind. Up here, it blows west to east.
Narrator
Europe's wind has just crossed a whole ocean. And oceans hold summer heat into winter. A giant hot-water bottle.
Narrator
New York's wind has just crossed a frozen continent.
Narrator
Then the Rockies make it worse.
Chars
[deadpan, slow, defensive] Don't look at me. I'm just standing here.
Narrator
They bend the jet stream. Arctic air down onto eastern America... mild air up toward Europe.
Narrator
So the Gulf Stream helps. But Europe's real heater? Where its wind has been.
Chars
[smug, unbothered] Still taking all the credit, though.
Narrator
This is Bhoogol. Follow for more Geography Fun Facts.
